can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the '-est' suffix, with adjectives of one syllable, and with two-syllable adjectives ending in -y.

ontology.mental_model: the -est / -iest suffix stamps a word as rank-one on a scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: y becomes i before you crown it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades things to the top rung

positives: He is the smartest boy in the class.
This is the easiest way to learn.
negatives: I will do my honest work.
They went into the dark forest.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'my' or 'your' + superlative adjective + noun, with a limited range of nouns and contexts. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: a possessive determiner hands the top rank to a person
ontology.agency_or_distance: possessive ties the superlative to an involved party

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjective phrases using 'the most', with longer adjectives of two or more syllables.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the most + adjective — stamp a multi-syllable adjective as rank-one
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades two-plus-syllable adjectives to the top

positives: It was the most beautiful day of my life.
This is the most expensive car here.
negatives: He took the most of the food.
That is the most biggest problem.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'the' + superlative adjective + noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: 'the' plus a -est adjective flags exactly one noun as peak of its kind
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker presents the ranking as given, unique

positives: It is the tallest building in town.
She is the best player on the team.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the suffix '-st' to adjectives ending in '–e'.

ontology.mental_model: words already ending in e just add -st to reach top rank
ontology.pedagogical_hook: late -> the latest: keep the e, add -st
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades to the extreme using e-final stems

positives: That is the largest building in the city.
She is the nicest person I know.
negatives: He is very honest about it.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('usually', 'often', 'never', 'weekly') to talk about frequency.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: usually / often / never / weekly — finer-grained frequency markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions the event on a denser frequency scale

positives: I usually walk to the park.
negatives: He gave me a daily task.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs ('so', 'quite', 'too') to modify adjectives.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: so / quite / too + adjective — turn the adjective up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker sets the adjective's intensity on a non-default position

positives: He was so tired after work.
negatives: I was late, so I ran home.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives ('main', 'only') that limit the noun that they go before.

ontology.mental_model: limiter fences the noun down to one

positives: This is the main reason I am here.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of manner adverbs and adverb phrases to modify how something happens.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: well / straight / slowly — describe HOW the action is performed
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker sculpts the texture of the verb's action

positives: She sings very well on stage.
negatives: Well, I think you are right.
It was a very deep well.
